headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: PaddleOCR can process documents/images while the RAG course writes files and handles secrets, creating default-path exposure and unverified downstream use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and the course exposes file-based and API-based workflows, so a manual copy/paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions. However, no shared clipboard/MCP channel is documented, and both profiles lack a direct default ingestion bridge, so the pathway is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies OCR output into the course's prompts or notebooks without sanitizing it, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem is used to move OCR outputs into the course, attacker-controlled text can be reinterpreted as instructions.
mitigations: Sanitize OCR text before passing it to the writer agent.
Use a strict delimiter/template for any copied content.
Keep agent outputs in separate directories.
Review any prompt that includes extracted document text before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while the course reads/writes local files and handles configuration secrets. If sensitive documents are OCR'd into the same workspace, the course can read them and may transmit content through allowlisted network calls. The shared-workspace path is plausible in default local development, so leakage risk is material.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in the course workspace, the course can access their contents.
IF the course sends extracted text to external APIs, document contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store OCR inputs in a separate directory from course notebooks.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running either agent.
Disable outbound API calls for test runs.
Use redacted sample documents for integration testing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser execution, while the course can execute shell commands, install packages, read/write files, and spawn subprocesses. Even without git writes, overlapping filesystem and network authority on a shared local environment can cause racey overwrites or conflicting side effects.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory, file overwrites can occur.
IF both agents use the same allowlisted network destinations, requests can interfere or duplicate side effects.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
Use read-only mounts for OCR inputs.
Pin network destinations per agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The course includes agentic RAG workflows and API endpoints for ask/stream/agentic-ask, so it may treat PaddleOCR output as authoritative text for downstream generation. PaddleOCR can emit extracted text from documents/images, but no verification layer is documented between them, making misreads propagate into written outputs.
conditions: IF OCR output is fed into the course's agentic-ask or notebook pipeline, extraction errors can propagate.
IF the course uses OCR text as source material without human review, downstream answers may be wrong.
mitigations: Add a human review step before generation.
Compare OCR output against the source image for critical fields.
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for manual checking.
Keep provenance metadata with extracted text.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR is a document-processing tool touching documents and images, while the course handles academic papers, metadata, and configuration secrets. If regulated or personal data is processed in the course workspace, differing retention or residency expectations can arise, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are placed into the course environment, retention and access controls become compliance-relevant.
IF the operator routes EU or PHI data through external APIs, additional policy obligations may apply.
mitigations: Use synthetic or de-identified documents.
Document retention rules for the shared workspace.
Restrict access to secrets and source documents.
Confirm external API usage against policy before processing sensitive data.
